feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations roles. Writing is polished overall, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization show trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Strong strategic/technical blend: combines digital strategy, CMS/platform work, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that feels senior and marketable.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional tone with good use of specifics like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scale: include results such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign impact.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix consistency/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; maintain consistent serial comma usage (“workflows, and systems” is awkward); standardize punctuation in bullets and section formatting. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that reflect the most recent web/platform modernization work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and lead with the current positioning: “Digital communications and strategy leader…”
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with “enterprise web, content, email, social, and multimedia operations” for a more senior tone.
- Add one high-value differentiator from recent roles, such as Drupal/CMS modernization, analytics infrastructure, or governance/workflow design.
- Tighten the final sentence to emphasize audience impact: translating policy and technical issues into accessible, action-oriented content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely repeat Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep the intro higher-level.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” also recur elsewhere, so avoid overloading the summary with skill-list language.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making it more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and tighten wording: Digital strategy & platform transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial operations & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Systems architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Change “communication” to “communications” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Replace vague terms like “administration” with stronger, more senior wording such as “management” or “governance.”
- Consider emphasizing higher-level leadership over execution if targeting senior roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy,” “analytics,” “workflow/systems,” and “multimedia” are already covered in more detail in Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and the Recent Projects section. Make it more outcome-led and frame it as post-director consulting focused on modernization initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advising NACo on post-migration digital modernization across Drupal, content operations, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled search.”
- Collapse overlapping duties into 3–4 high-impact bullets; lead with initiatives delivered, not generic consulting language.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/templates/toolkits launched, workflow time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains, stakeholders supported, or issues resolved.
- Tighten phrasing, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits for national advocacy initiatives.
- Improved cross-channel content workflows, analytics, and governance supporting coordinated web, email, social, and multimedia publishing.
- Led AI-enabled search strategy, including retrieval design, structured content models, and discovery UX.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats prior NACo roles; only keep if tied to new consulting outcomes.
- Microsite and AI search details duplicate Recent Projects; summarize here and let projects carry specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in the adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Combine the website bullets and foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, production volume, cost savings, or campaign impact for email/social/video if available; otherwise shorten.
- Tighten operations language: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio and expanded analytics across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting, governance and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this one strategic, not day-to-day.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles; emphasize building the studio/capability rather than recurring production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level: operating cadence, editorial coordination, and channel expansion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Sharpen the video bullet: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one outcome-oriented line: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not introducing it.
- “Digital operations across web, email, social” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; avoid broad leadership phrasing here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector stakeholder engagement
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Stakeholder engagement” or “Mission-driven communications” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Keep this section capability-focused; save outcomes like website scale, publisher count, and audience reach for recent experience bullets where they carry more impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” closely duplicate the header and Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeats language already demonstrated in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a raw keyword list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to web modernization and platform delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal/CMS modernization first; it aligns best with the most recent and highest-impact work.
- Consider dropping one lower-signal item if space is tight; “WordPress” is less central than Drupal given recent experience.
- If you want more impact, make it outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization and technical delivery” as the heading, with fewer, sharper terms underneath.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep this version broader and more strategic, not a second full tools list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid overemphasizing it here unless it’s a target-role differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic value and decision-making more than platform names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with a broader, impact-oriented phrase like “search, content and conversion performance analysis.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive reporting dashboards • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • Search, content & user-performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- Since recent NACo experience already names these tools, avoid repeating the full stack here unless this section is shortened and made more strategic.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent leadership-level production capabilities rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more outcome-oriented, senior phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production & editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production systems
- Virtual event and advocacy content delivery
- Consider dropping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the studio buildout and leadership scope.
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing tools, formats, and responsibilities in inconsistent terms.
- If space is tight, reduce to 4 bullets by combining virtual/hybrid event delivery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- Tool-level detail here also overlaps with Technical + IT (“Livestream studio workflows,” Premiere Pro, Audition).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a bare inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is the strongest and most recent platform in the experience section, lead with that and add light context or proficiency signals.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” → put Drupal first and consider grouping as “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; Static publishing: GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add level/context: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular builds) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Consider tightening the title to “CMS & Web Platforms” for more natural phrasing.
- If you want stronger impact, replace one lower-value item with a more differentiating capability already evidenced in experience, e.g., “Drupal • CMS modernization • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates Topline Skills [2] almost exactly; keep one as platform names only and the other as broader capabilities.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so don’t repeat it here unless you remove it from Topline Skills.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. It should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools while staying concise.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- Consider grouping by function for readability: **Front-end:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery | **Implementation:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager | **Infrastructure/CI:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If space allows, add a light proficiency cue tied to recent work, e.g. **Front-end implementation for Drupal-based public websites, campaign microsites, and workflow automation**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** and **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- If keeping both sections, use Topline Skills for broad themes and this item only for specific tools/platforms.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and grouped around systems leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Group by function for faster scanning: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were used at scale recently, add light context elsewhere, not here, e.g. “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable and Power Automate” or “managed editorial/project operations across Jira and Asana.”
- Consider trimming to the strongest, most relevant tools: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Microsoft Teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating both concepts verbatim.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar; listing all four may feel padded unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and misses the scale/context already shown in recent NACo roles. It would be stronger if framed around enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than basic email marketing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and modernize the list: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show level without repeating work-history detail, e.g. **enterprise newsletter and member-engagement platforms**
- Consider ordering by strategic weight/relevance: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** (keep Mailchimp last as the least enterprise-oriented)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email/newsletter references in Work Experience; keep this section tool-focused only, not outcome-focused.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid adding broad channel language here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer outcomes and less emphasis on leadership that is better demonstrated in 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to stress early-team build and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the close to: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates, supported a major website refresh, and coordinated day-to-day execution with a digital media associate.”
- If metrics exist, include 1–2: “delivered X livestreams/year,” “supported Y% traffic growth,” or “reduced production time by Z%.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on building/launching rather than scaling.
- “Providing day-to-day guidance” may feel redundant with later management leadership unless framed as informal coordination.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams.”
- Make the second sentence more active and specific: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Consider a one-line version for concision: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives while producing digital content and launching NACo’s first podcast.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats later roles; keep this item focused on innovation/research support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.
